title: Grade 9 Science — Structure of Atom & Cell
description: Structure of the Atom and Cell — Fundamental Unit of Life practice questions
subject: science

questions.question: The nucleus of an atom contains:
questions.explanation: The nucleus contains protons (positively charged) and neutrons (no charge). Electrons are found in orbits (shells) around the nucleus.

questions.question: The atomic number of an element is equal to the number of:
questions.explanation: Atomic number (Z) = number of protons in the nucleus. For a neutral atom, it also equals the number of electrons.

questions.question: In Bohr's model of the atom, electrons can only be in orbits with:
options: Increasing energy as they get closer to nucleus
questions.explanation: Bohr's atomic model proposed that electrons exist only in fixed, discrete orbits (shells) around the nucleus. Each orbit has a specific energy level.

questions.question: The maximum number of electrons in the third shell (M shell) of an atom is:
questions.explanation: Maximum electrons in any shell n = 2n². For n = 3 (M shell): 2 × 3² = 18. For n=1: 2, n=2: 8.

questions.question: Isotopes of an element have the same number of protons but different numbers of:
questions.explanation: Isotopes are atoms of the same element with the same atomic number (same protons) but different mass numbers due to different numbers of neutrons. Example: ¹²C and ¹⁴C.

questions.question: The atomic mass of an element is approximately equal to:
options: Number of protons + number of neutrons
Number of neutrons − number of protons
questions.explanation: Atomic mass (mass number) = protons + neutrons. Electrons have negligible mass. For example, carbon-12 has 6 protons + 6 neutrons = mass number 12.

questions.question: The valency of an element with 7 electrons in the outermost shell is:
questions.explanation: Valency = 8 − (outermost electrons) if outermost electrons > 4. 8 − 7 = 1. This element (like chlorine) gains 1 electron to complete its octet.

questions.question: Which scientist proposed the nuclear model of the atom based on the gold foil experiment?
questions.explanation: Rutherford's gold foil (alpha particle scattering) experiment (1911) showed that most of an atom is empty space with a tiny, dense, positively charged nucleus.

questions.question: The basic structural and functional unit of life is:
questions.explanation: The cell is the basic unit of life. All living things are made of one or more cells, and all life processes occur within cells.

questions.question: The powerhouse of the cell is the:
questions.explanation: Mitochondria are called the powerhouse of the cell because they produce ATP (adenosine triphosphate) through cellular respiration, providing energy for cellular activities.

questions.question: Plant cells have a cell wall made of:
questions.explanation: Plant cell walls are made of cellulose, a rigid polysaccharide. The cell wall provides structural support and maintains cell shape. Animal cells do not have cell walls.

questions.question: Which organelle controls all activities of the cell and contains genetic material?
questions.explanation: The nucleus controls all cell activities and contains DNA (genetic material). It is the control centre of the cell, enclosed by the nuclear envelope.

questions.question: Prokaryotic cells differ from eukaryotic cells in that they:
options: Have a defined nucleus with a nuclear membrane
questions.explanation: Prokaryotic cells (bacteria, blue-green algae) have no membrane-bound nucleus — their genetic material floats freely in the cytoplasm. Eukaryotic cells have a well-defined nucleus.

questions.question: Chloroplasts are found in plant cells and are responsible for:
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and are the sites of photosynthesis — converting light energy, water, and CO₂ into glucose and oxygen.

questions.question: The process by which a cell takes in large particles or droplets by engulfing them with its membrane is called:
questions.explanation: Endocytosis is the process by which cells engulf large particles (phagocytosis) or fluid (pinocytosis) by wrapping the plasma membrane around them to form a vesicle inside the cell.
